race_context: The district: Silver Creek School Corporation, based in Sellersburg in Clark County, runs four schools: Silver Creek Primary (K-1), Silver Creek Elementary (2-5), Silver Creek Middle (6-8) and Silver Creek High (9-12) {scsc_news}{scsc_home}. It split from the former West Clark Community Schools, along with Borden and Henryville schools, in 2020 {lpm_ref_result}. State data show 3,189 students in 2026, up from 2,799 in 2021 {idoe_enroll}.
Superintendent: Dr. Chad Briggs. Dr. Todd Balmer is assistant superintendent and CFO {scsc_staff}.

Board: five members, Chris Rountree, Scott Groan, Kristy Franklin, Joe Basham and Laurryn McDaniel {scsc_board}. Three are elected from districts: Rountree (District 1), Groan (District 2) and McDaniel (District 3) won those seats in 2024 {enr_2024}{lpm_2024}. The other two seats are at-large. Basham and Franklin won them in 2022, when the state results show two seats and only those two candidates; Basham got 2,618 votes and Franklin 2,253 {enr_2022}. The district website does not list officer roles or term dates {scsc_board}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the state list shows 'vote for 1' {in_list}. But the two at-large seats were filled together in 2022 (state results: two seats) and in 2020, when the News and Tribune reported 'two At-large seats open' {enr_2022}{nt_2020}. With four-year terms, both 2022 terms appear to end in 2026, so this guide believes the race elects TWO members. If so, the two candidates on the ballot would fill both seats. This guide did not find an official 2026 seat count, so voters should check their sample ballot.

Who is running: both at-large incumbents are on the ballot and no one else filed. Louisville Public Media listed Joseph W. 'Joe' Basham as Independent and Kristy Franklin as nonpartisan {lpm_2026}{in_list}. LPM noted that 2026 is the first general election in which school board candidates can run with a party label under a 2025 state law, and that most candidates still chose to run as nonpartisan {lpm_2026}.

Building capacity and the failed referendum (May 2025): the board asked voters to approve a property tax referendum of up to $62.86 million over 25 years. It would have paid for a new elementary school and fieldhouse, more classrooms at the primary school (pre-K, kindergarten, first grade and special education), classroom changes at the elementary and middle schools, and HVAC, roofing and paving work at the high school {lpm_ref_preview}. LPM reported that the primary, elementary and middle schools were all over their best capacity as of fall 2024. The measure would have raised residential property taxes paid to the district by an average of 44.13% and business property taxes by 32.56% {lpm_ref_preview}.

Referendum result: voters rejected it on May 6, 2025, 3,759 (94%) to 238 (nearly 6%), with 12,356 registered voters eligible {lpm_ref_result}. Assistant Superintendent and CFO Todd Balmer said, 'We know we've got to still look at creating capacity.' He said the district would 'take a step back' and look at other options, and LPM reported that modular classrooms were one immediate option {lpm_ref_result}. A resident who opposed the measure ran a Facebook page called 'No To Silver Creek Tax Hikes' {lpm_ref_result}. This guide found no news report of a replacement building plan.

Town funding proposal (September 2026): the Town of Sellersburg's redevelopment commission was considering a partnership with the school corporation. Commission Vice President Patrick Duggins proposed using tax-increment financing (TIF) money, which state law lets commissions spend on educational and job-training programs {nt_tif}. The rest of the article is for subscribers only, so the outcome is not reported here.
Budget and SEA 1: this guide found no public statement from the board or district on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Silver Creek's budget.
Forums: this guide found no candidate forum, questionnaire or campaign coverage for this race. With two candidates for what appear to be two seats, the race may not be contested.

candidates.summary: Incumbent at-large board member, first elected in 2020 when the district held its first board election, and listed as an Independent {enr_2020}{enr_2022}{scsc_board}{in_list}.
background: A 2018 Clark County REMC candidate profile described him as a mechanical supervisor at Lehigh Hanson Cement in Speed and a 1973 graduate of Silver Creek High School. It said he took millwright classes at Ivy Tech Community College and had coached cross country at Silver Creek Middle School for 30 years {remc_2018}.

The same 2018 profile said he was a member of the West Clark Community School Board (the district Silver Creek later split from) and the Indiana School Board Association, and was 'recognized as master board member' {remc_2018}.
Serves as District Four director on the Clark County REMC board. A 2024 co-op profile said he has lived in the Perry Crossing area of Carr Township for more than 30 years {remc_2024}{remc_2018}.
path_to_ballot: Won an at-large seat in 2020, the new district's first board election, finishing second of three candidates with 3,268 votes; the News and Tribune reported that two at-large seats were open {enr_2020}{nt_2020}.
Re-elected in 2022 with 2,618 votes in an uncontested race for two at-large seats {enr_2022}.
Filed for 2026 and is listed as an Independent {lpm_2026}{in_list}.
on_incumbent: Is a current board member {scsc_board}. This guide found no public statement from him on the board's record, including the 2025 referendum.
